statement: An MCP capability that promises artifacts from the most recent scan must be tested across the transport's real request lifecycle, not only through a persistent in-process server. Occurrence 2026-09-27: Cejel's HTTP handler constructs a fresh MCP server for every request, so a successful `scan` stores `lastScan` in a discarded instance and a later HTTP `resources/read` fails with "No scan has run yet". Require an end-to-end scan-then-resource-read test using separate HTTP requests; either make the transport explicitly stateless and return artifacts with the scan result, or define bounded, authenticated session state before advertising last-scan resources.

movesWhen.reason: Await a Cejel fix that aligns HTTP MCP artifact resources with the request lifecycle and adds a separate-request regression test.
